_note: Ratchet for static-only feature contracts under tests/features/ — files that read source with assertIncludes/assertMatches (tests/helpers/feature-test-harness.mjs) but never execute real app code. 253 static contracts stayed green while 20 route commands were dead, a Finder list overflowed in all six eras, and Control Panel could not be typed into — a static contract reads the shape of the source, it cannot see wiring. staticOnlyFeatureContracts is the count at baseline (2026-09-01, tests/features/action-registry-dispatch.test.mjs's lane — 278 feature test files total, 103 already executing real app code via node:vm or a shared VM harness, 175 static-only; lowered to 174 on 2026-09-03 when the executing signal learned that a test which spawns apps/server/server.js and drives it over HTTP executes the product more completely than a VM harness does) and verify fails if the current count rises above it. To add a new feature test: execute real app code instead — tests/helpers/app-boot-vm.mjs (boots the eager module set in a VM, dispatches real actions, opens real windows, loads real lazy modules), draft-desk-vm.mjs / write-lease-vm.mjs / backup-vm.mjs (narrower existing VM harnesses), or vm.runInContext directly the way ~100 existing tests already do. To lower the budget: convert an existing static contract to an executing one (or delete/merge it into one that already executes the same path), then edit this number down in the same commit. To raise it: only in a commit whose description justifies why the new contract genuinely cannot execute anything (e.g. a pure data/translation-parity check) — the same rule tooling/css-budget.json uses for its own ratchets.
